claims.text: A machine-learned interatomic potential combined with free-energy perturbation can reproduce explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics accuracy for fusion and high-temperature thermodynamic properties.
The proposed ML-plus-perturbation workflow will cost substantially less than explicit ab initio molecular dynamics.
Crystalline and molten coordinates or key thermodynamic data are partially known for a suitable quaternary or quinary HEA such as Al-Cr-Co-Fe-Ni.
A small set of ab initio snapshots near melting is sufficient to train the proposed flexible machine-learning potential.
Residual potential errors can be corrected by free-energy perturbation against high-fidelity DFT data from both solid and liquid phases.
An interatomic potential can represent multicomponent interactions in quinary Al-Cr-Co-Fe-Ni and produce first-principles-consistent high-temperature structural behavior.
The ML potential will determine sufficiently accurate atomic forces and energies in both crystalline and liquid states.
The ML potential can capture electronic contributions to vibrational and anharmonic entropy.
Training on representative ab initio data allows the ML potential to reproduce short- and medium-range bonding physics.
Free-energy perturbation corrects local errors in the ML potential.
The proposed correction captures electron-vibration coupling accurately enough to yield reliable phase free energies.
The workflow will reduce computational cost by at least fivefold relative to full ab initio molecular dynamics.
The workflow will reduce computational cost by at least fivefold relative to TOR-TILD.
Predicted phase-transition temperatures will agree with ab initio benchmarks within a few tens of kelvin.
Predicted phase free energies will agree with ab initio benchmarks within a few meV per atom.
The method is effective for compositionally complex alloys containing up to five principal elements.
The claimed operating range extends from approximately 0.5 to 1.5 times the melting temperature.
The method is applicable at near-ambient or moderately elevated pressures relevant to fusion-reactor conditions.
Transfer outside the training range and application to strongly magnetic or highly anisotropic systems may require additional validation.
Deviations exceeding approximately 5 meV per atom in phase free energy or 30–50 K in melting temperature across multiple temperatures would falsify the hypothesis.
